# ADR-0806 — .github/workflows/mcp-toplist-badge.yml

Source rationale preserved verbatim. Identifiers inside historical quotations are not current identities.

## .github/workflows/mcp-toplist-badge.yml — original line 3

````text
# assets/badge-mcp-toplist.svg is a committed static file rather than a
# hotlinked remote image, so its claim cannot be restated without a commit
# here. The cost of that choice is that the badge cannot self-update: the
# date it carries is part of the claim and goes stale by INACTION, and
# inaction never opens a PR. This workflow is what closes that loop.
````

## .github/workflows/mcp-toplist-badge.yml — original line 9

````text
# Monthly, not weekly: the badge stamps a month, so a monthly run is the
# least frequent cadence that keeps the date honest and the most frequent
# one that does not churn a PR proposing an identical file.
````

## .github/workflows/mcp-toplist-badge.yml — original line 13

````text
# No pull_request trigger on purpose. The script reads a third-party site;
# wiring that into PR CI would make a required check depend on someone
# else's uptime. The unit tests in tests_py/scripts/ cover the logic and
# run in the normal suite with no network at all.
````

## .github/workflows/mcp-toplist-badge.yml — original line 55

````text
#   1. GitHub deliberately does not trigger `pull_request`/`push`
#      workflows on PRs opened by GITHUB_TOKEN — so main's required
#      checks never start and the PR cannot be merged until a
#      maintainer pushes to the branch (a re-run, an empty commit, or
#      closing/reopening the PR).
#   2. Independently of (1), the repo/org policy at Settings → Actions
#      → General → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
#      requests" gates PR *creation* itself. With that box unchecked,
#      this step fails outright with "GitHub Actions is not permitted
#      to create or approve pull requests" — no PR, no branch left
#      pushed (peter-evans/create-pull-request pushes the branch
#      first, then fails the PR-creation call; the branch must be
#      deleted by hand). See issue #273. That box was checked
#      2026-07-30 to fix this; if it is ever unchecked again (a repo
#      transfer, an org policy reset), set BADGE_REFRESH_TOKEN to a
#      PAT with `repo` scope instead — the workflow already prefers
#      it — which sidesteps both (1) and (2) since a PAT-authored PR
#      is not GITHUB_TOKEN-authored.
````
